-- ══ The two bag verbs benilla answers differently ═════════════════════════════════════ -- Deviation: `OpenBackpack` opens every equipped bag, not only the backpack, so the vendor -- and mailbox windows that call it (MerchantFrame.lua:35, MailFrame.lua:39) bring up every -- bag to sell or mail from. The was-open memory is keyed by bag id: `ContainerFrame1..12` -- are recycled across bags. The stock `CloseAllBags` (ContainerFrame.lua:702-707) runs -- unchanged: it calls this `CloseBackpack`, then closes bags 1 and up. BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN = {}
-- The reference's `backpackWasOpen`, one entry per bag: CloseBackpack leaves those open. function BenillaOpenBackpack() for bagId = 0, (NUM_BAG_FRAMES or -1) do -- OpenBag's own test, repeated so the memory agrees with it. if bagId == 0 or GetContainerNumSlots(bagId) > 0 then if IsBagOpen(bagId) then BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] = 1 else BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] = nil OpenBag(bagId) end end end end
function BenillaCloseBackpack() for bagId = 0, (NUM_BAG_FRAMES or -1) do if not BENILLA_BAG_WAS_OPEN[bagId] then CloseBag(bagId) end end end
-- The stock names, redefined after the stock ContainerFrame.lua has loaded, so its callers -- (the vendor and mailbox windows, the vendor's close and `CloseAllBags`) reach these. OpenBackpack = BenillaOpenBackpack CloseBackpack = BenillaCloseBackpack
